title: Instant Pot Egg Curry
equip: Instant Pot with trivet, stainless steel bowl, Philips hand blender (stick)

items.sub: 3 onion-tomato masala cubes (then skip the tomato and halve the sauté time)

items.n: green chilli, slit (remove before blending for kids)
kasuri methi, crushed between your palms

steps.x: Set the Instant Pot to Sauté (High). Heat the oil, add cumin and bay leaf for 30 sec.
Add the onion and cook 6 min until light golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli for 1 min, then the tomato for 3 min until soft.
Stir in all the ground spices and salt for 1 min. Pour in the water and scrape the bottom completely so there's no burn warning.
Set the trivet in the pot over the curry and put the eggs in the steel bowl (or straight on the trivet). The steam from the curry cooks them.
Lock the lid with the vent on Sealing. Pressure cook on High for 5 min, natural release for 5 min, then release the rest.
Move the eggs into a bowl of cold water for 5 min, then peel. Halve them lengthwise.
Lift out the trivet and the bay leaf (and the green chilli, if the kids are eating). Blend the curry with the hand blender until smooth.
Set to Sauté. Add the halved eggs and kasuri methi and simmer 3 min, spooning gravy over the eggs. Turn off and stir in lime juice and coriander.

notes: Approx. per portion (3 eggs + gravy): 310 kcal, 20g protein. Lighter on protein than the chicken lunches: add 200g paneer cubes or 1 can of drained chickpeas in the last step, or pack 100g Greek yogurt on the side.
Halve the eggs before packing. Whole boiled eggs can burst in the microwave.
Fridge: 3 days. Don't freeze; the eggs go rubbery.
Reheat 2 min, stir, then 30 sec more.
